s: Who translated the Bible into Telugu in 1746–47?
x:
Benjamin Schulz (Benjamin Schultze), a German Lutheran missionary associated with the Danish-Halle Mission, was the first person to translate the Bible into Telugu during 1746–47. Recognizing the need to communicate Christian teachings in the local language, he mastered Telugu and undertook the translation of the Bible. His work became a landmark in the history of Telugu prose and printing. The translation also contributed to the development of modern Telugu literature by introducing prose style and encouraging the publication of printed books. Benjamin Schulz's contribution extended beyond religious literature. He also prepared Telugu grammars and dictionaries, helping European scholars understand the Telugu language. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• First Telugu Bible Translator – Benjamin Schulz
• Period – 1746–47
• Contribution – Early Telugu prose and Christian literature

s: Which European power first established a factory at Machilipatnam?
x:
The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish commercial contacts and a trading factory at Machilipatnam. They reached the Coromandel Coast soon after the discovery of the sea route to India by Vasco da Gama in 1498. Later, the Dutch, English and French also established trading factories at Machilipatnam because of its thriving textile trade and strategic location on the east coast. Machilipatnam subsequently became one of the busiest ports on the Coromandel Coast and an important centre for international trade. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

s: Where did the English establish their first factory in Coastal Andhra?
x:
Machilipatnam (Masulipatnam) was the first trading factory established by the English East India Company in Coastal Andhra in 1611. It was one of the busiest ports on the Coromandel Coast and served as an important centre for the export of textiles, indigo and spices. The English obtained permission from the Qutb Shahi rulers of Golconda to establish this factory. From Machilipatnam, the Company gradually expanded its commercial activities to other parts of South India, eventually laying the foundation for British political dominance. The port remained an important centre of international trade for the English, Dutch and French throughout the seventeenth century. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• First English Factory in Andhra – Machilipatnam (1611)
• Permission granted by – Qutb Shahi rulers
• Major Export – Cotton textiles

s: The famous seaport town of the Kakatiyas?
x:
Motupalli, situated in present-day Bapatla district, was the principal seaport of the Kakatiya Kingdom. It served as an important centre for overseas trade with countries such as Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, Arabia and China. The famous Motupalli Charter of Ganapatideva granted protection and commercial privileges to foreign merchants, encouraging maritime trade. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Kakatiya Port – Motupalli
• Famous Inscription – Motupalli Charter of Ganapatideva

s: Which one of the following was an important seaport in the Kakatiya Kingdom?
x: Motupalli (Desiyakondapattanam) was the most important Kakatiya port; Machilipatnam was the Qutb Shahi port, so it is the tempting wrong option.

s: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
x: Motupalli had served as an international port during the early and medieval periods. Italian traveller Marco Polo, who had visited the port in 1287 AD, had given a vivid account of the flourishing trade activities at the port during the reign of Kakatiya queen Rudrama Devi. Inscriptions of Kakatiya Ganapathi Deva, Anapotha Reddy of the Kondaveedu dynasty and Deva Raya II of the Vijayanagara dynasty mention the port and the incentives provided to the sea-borne traders.

s: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
x: Motupalli was the famous trading seaport of the Kakatiyas. Marco Polo visited Kakatiya kingdom through this port and wrote about the prosperity and power in Andhra Desh in his travelogue.

s: Carnatic War was fought between :
x: The First Carnatic War (1746-48 A.D.) was an offshoot of the Anglo-French rivalry in the Austrian War of succession that took place in Europe in 1740 AD. The British Commodore Bernett captured some French ships which became the immediate cause of the war. Nawab Anwaruddin sent an army under the command of Mahfooz Khan to besiege the French in Madras during the first Carnatic War. The French Army (under the command of Captain Paradise) defeated Nawab’s Army at the Battle of St. Thome near Adyar river. Treaty of Aix-La-Chapelle (18 Oct, 1748 A.D.) ended the War of Austrian succession and with it first Carnatic War ended and the Britishers reoccupied Madras. The first Carnatic War is memorable for the War of St. Thome.

s: The immediate cause of the first Carnatic war was
o: capturing of French naval fleet by English.
x: The immediate trigger was the English navy's seizure of French ships, which led France to retaliate. The War of Austrian Succession and Anglo-French rivalry were the wider background, not the immediate cause.

s: What is/are not true in relation to 'Battle of Ambur'? (i) This battle was fought in 1752. (ii) In this battle, armies of Muzaffarjang, Chanda Sahib and French fought together against Anwarud-din. (iii) In this battle, army of Anwar-ud-din had to face defeat.
